groups.name: Across the Golden Gate: Marin and the redwoods
Around the bay and down the coast

neighborhoods.name: Union Square and downtown
neighborhoods.tip: The hotel and shopping center of the city. Cable cars start at Powell and Market; BART and Muni Metro run under Market Street.

neighborhoods.name: Fisherman's Wharf
neighborhoods.tip: On the north waterfront, near the bay cruises, Pier 39 and both Powell cable car lines. The F streetcar runs along the Embarcadero to the Ferry Building.

neighborhoods.name: Embarcadero and Financial District
neighborhoods.tip: Flat, by the water, close to the Ferry Building and the ferries. BART and Muni stop at Embarcadero station.

neighborhoods.name: North Beach and Telegraph Hill
neighborhoods.tip: Walkable to Chinatown, Coit Tower and the wharf. Hilly to the east.

neighborhoods.name: Chinatown
neighborhoods.tip: Between Union Square and North Beach. The Central Subway stops at Chinatown-Rose Pak station.

neighborhoods.name: Nob Hill and Russian Hill
neighborhoods.tip: Grand hotels at the top of very steep streets. All three cable car lines cross here, which saves the climb.

neighborhoods.name: South of Market
neighborhoods.tip: Flat and central, near SFMOMA, the convention center and the ballpark.

neighborhoods.name: Marina and Cow Hollow
neighborhoods.tip: Flat streets by the bay, near the Palace of Fine Arts and Crissy Field. Buses rather than trains.

neighborhoods.name: Hayes Valley and Civic Center
neighborhoods.tip: Near City Hall, the opera and the symphony. Civic Center has BART and Muni Metro.

neighborhoods.name: Pacific Heights and Japantown
neighborhoods.tip: Quiet, grand houses and Fillmore Street shops, with Japantown just south. Buses and taxis.

neighborhoods.name: The Mission and the Castro
neighborhoods.tip: Sunny, lively and flat, with BART at 16th and 24th Street and Muni Metro at Castro.

neighborhoods.name: Haight-Ashbury and Golden Gate Park
neighborhoods.tip: At the east end of Golden Gate Park. The N Judah streetcar runs downtown.

neighborhoods.name: Richmond, Sunset and the ocean
neighborhoods.tip: Residential and often foggy, between the park, the Presidio and Ocean Beach. Allow 30 to 40 minutes to downtown by bus or streetcar.

neighborhoods.name: Sausalito and Marin
neighborhoods.tip: Across the Golden Gate Bridge. The ferry to the Ferry Building takes about 30 minutes; check the last sailing.

neighborhoods.name: Oakland and Berkeley
neighborhoods.tip: Across the Bay Bridge. BART reaches downtown San Francisco in 15 to 25 minutes.

neighborhoods.name: The Peninsula and Silicon Valley
neighborhoods.tip: South of the city. BART serves the airport area and Millbrae; Caltrain runs down to Palo Alto and San Jose.

airports.name: San Francisco airport (SFO)
airports.tip: BART leaves from the International Terminal and reaches downtown in about 30 minutes. Taxis use the meter plus a $6 airport pick-up fee.

airports.name: Oakland airport (OAK)
airports.tip: Take BART from the airport to Coliseum station, then a San Francisco train to one of the four downtown stations.

airports.name: San Jose airport (SJC)
airports.tip: About an hour south by car. Best if you are staying in Silicon Valley.

items.title: Tap your card or phone
items.text: On Muni buses, streetcars and Metro, on BART and on the Golden Gate ferries, tap a contactless credit or debit card, or your phone or watch, on the reader. Each rider needs their own card or device. No app or transit card needed.

items.title: Muni: buses, streetcars and Metro
items.text: One adult ride is $2.85 when you tap, $3.00 in cash (exact change), and covers transfers for two hours. A Day Pass is $5.70 and does not include cable cars. Age 18 and under ride free on Muni, except cable cars.

items.title: Cable cars
items.text: $9 a ride, with no transfers. From 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. at the three main turnarounds (Powell and Market, Bay and Taylor, Hyde and Beach), buy your fare before boarding. Children 4 and under ride free.

items.title: Visitor Passport
items.text: Unlimited Muni rides including cable cars: $15 for one day, with 3-day and 7-day versions too. Worth it from the second cable car ride. It is not valid on BART or to the airport.

items.title: BART and the airports
items.text: From SFO, the station is in the International Terminal; the free AirTrain connects the other terminals. Downtown is about 30 minutes. Tap in and tap out with the same card. Trains from SFO run from 4:58 a.m. on weekdays, 5:47 a.m. on Saturdays and 8:08 a.m. on Sundays, until midnight. Fares depend on distance: use the fare calculator on bart.gov.

items.title: Ferries
items.text: Golden Gate Ferry sails from behind the Ferry Building (gates B and C) to Sausalito, Larkspur, Tiburon and Angel Island. A paper ticket to Sausalito is $14 one way; tapping a card or Clipper costs less. No service on New Year's Day, Thanksgiving or Christmas Day.

items.title: Driverless cars
items.text: Waymo runs driverless taxis across the city, booked in the Waymo app like any ride app. Rides to and from SFO started in 2026, using the airport's Rental Car Center, with access widening in stages: check the app for what is offered on your dates.

items.title: The hills
items.text: Maps do not show how steep the city is. Two blocks can feel like ten. Wear flat shoes with grip, and use a bus, a cable car or a short taxi ride for the climbs. The waterfront from the Ferry Building to Fisherman's Wharf and Crissy Field is flat.

items.title: Do you need a car?
items.text: Not in the city, where parking is expensive and scarce. Rent one, or join a tour, for Muir Woods, wine country and the coast. Never leave anything visible in a parked car, not even for five minutes.

getting_around.source: SFMTA (fares, cable car, Visitor Passport, Tap to Pay), BART (SFO airport guide), Golden Gate Ferry (fares effective July 1, 2026), Waymo and SFO (airport service, January 2026)

taxis.intro_bold: San Francisco taxis run on the meter.
taxis.intro: Hail one with its roof light on, find one at hotels and the airport, or book through the Flywheel app, which the city's transport agency recommends for taxis. Passengers pay bridge tolls. There is no charge for luggage. Tip about 15 to 20%.
taxis.apps: Uber, Lyft and Waymo (driverless) all work in the city. Check the price in the app before you book.

taxi_tariff.rush_note: The meter adds $0.65 for each minute the taxi is stopped or crawling, so traffic costs more. Trips ending more than 15 miles beyond the city limits are charged at 150% of the meter, and bridge tolls are added.
taxi_tariff.note: Rough estimate from the city meter rates ($4.15 for the first fifth of a mile, then $0.65 for each further fifth, which is $3.25 a mile, shown here per km) and straight-line distance. The meter decides.
taxi_tariff.source: SFMTA Taxi Fares (rates in force since Nov 17, 2022)

rides.title: Drivers and rides
rides.intro: In the city, Muni, taxis and ride apps cover almost everything. For Muir Woods, wine country and the coast, rent a car or join a tour.

items.name: Taxis and the Flywheel app
items.what: Metered city taxis can be hailed on the street, called by phone or booked in the Flywheel app.

items.name: Waymo
items.what: Driverless taxis booked in the Waymo app. Airport rides use the SFO Rental Car Center.
